name: GLB improvement 2: assembly repair and adaptive best-of-N
description: Offline tooling that targets the main weakness the imp-ops numbers show: single-shot v3 assets are valid (about 90%) but only about 65% assembled, while best-of-3 reaches 100% valid and 87.5% assembled at 3x the time. Add (1) an assembly repair turn that tells the model which parts float or are disconnected, (2) a sequential best-of-N cost simulator that stops sampling at the first assembled valid candidate, (3) report columns over all briefs, (4) imp_ops.sh jobs for the follow-up.

userStories.title: Assembly repair mode in glb_repair.py
userStories.description: As a product user, I want a valid but badly assembled asset fed back once with what is wrong, because floating and disconnected parts are the main quality failure (docs/14 section 2).
steps: Add `--mode assembly` to scripts/glb_repair.py (default stays `error`, existing behaviour unchanged). Selection: rows in RUN_DIR/validation.jsonl with ok == true whose RUN_DIR/assembly.jsonl entry has assembly.assembled == false; skip rows with parts < 3.

Fix message: 'Your page works, but the exported model is not assembled: it has N separate groups of parts (largest group holds P% of the parts), F parts float in the air and the lowest point is G above the ground. Reply with the complete corrected HTML file in one ```html block. Keep the same design and parts; only move or resize parts so they touch their neighbours, sit on the ground (lowest y = 0), and keep it in one THREE.Group named "asset".' Numbers come from the assembly stats (percent and metres rounded to 2 decimals).

Outputs go to RUN_DIR/repair-asm/ (raw, glb, shots, validation.jsonl, summary.json {mode, selected, attempted, repaired, assembled_after, ids_repaired}). `repaired` counts rows that are still ok after repair; `assembled_after` counts those also assembled (read from the new validation rows' stats.glb.assembly). Resumable.

Tests: fake Ollama server; assert the 4-message order, the fix text contains the three numbers, rows with assembled true / not ok / parts < 3 are skipped, error mode selection is unchanged (existing tests still pass), re-run makes no new requests.
acceptanceCriteria: Fake-server test asserts the assembly fix message text with the group, percent, floater and ground numbers
Existing error-mode tests in tests/py/test_glb_repair.py still pass unchanged
Re-running makes no new HTTP requests for ids already written (asserted)
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

userStories.title: Sequential best-of-N cost simulator (glb_best_of_cost.py)
userStories.description: As the owner, I want to know how much of best-of-3's time an adaptive rule would save, using samples I already have.
steps: Create scripts/glb_best_of_cost.py --runs DIR [DIR ...] --briefs FILE [--out FILE.json]. Each run dir has validation.jsonl, assembly.jsonl (optional) and raw/<id>.json with a seconds field (use the same field glb_report.py reads for Median seconds).

Rule: for each brief walk the runs in the given order; stop at the first candidate that is ok and assembled (kind-aware assembly from assembly.jsonl); otherwise continue to the last run and pick with the same ranking glb_best_of.py uses (import it, do not copy it). Report: mean samples used per brief, mean and median seconds per brief, share ok, share assembled, versus always-3 (samples 3.0, seconds sum of all three).

Print a short table and write the JSON. Tests with tiny fixture runs (3 runs, 4 briefs) checking each number by hand: one brief stops at sample 1, one at 2, one never assembles (uses all 3, picks by ranking), one has no ok candidate.
acceptanceCriteria: Hand-computed expected values for the 4-brief fixture are asserted (samples used, seconds, shares)
The picker ranking is imported from glb_best_of.py, not duplicated (asserted by a test that monkeypatches it)
Missing assembly.jsonl for a run is handled: those rows count as not assembled, with a printed warning
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)

userStories.title: Report columns over all briefs
userStories.description: As the owner, I want assembly shown against all 48 briefs, not only the valid ones, so a model cannot look better by failing more.
steps: In scripts/glb_report.py add a column 'Assembled (of all briefs)' = assembled count / brief count next to the existing 'Assembled (of valid)'. Keep column order otherwise; update tests/py/test_glb_report.py with a fixture where the two denominators differ.

Support `--extra-runs NAME=DIR` where DIR is a `repair-asm` directory: label it '<model> after assembly repair'; its ok and assembled counts take the repaired rows' values where the repair was applied and the original rows elsewhere (ids from summary.json ids_repaired and the original run).
Document both in docs/14 section 3 in two sentences.
acceptanceCriteria: A fixture with 4 briefs, 3 ok, 2 assembled shows 2/3 of valid and 2/4 of all briefs (asserted)
The after-assembly-repair row merges original and repaired rows by id (asserted on a fixture)

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Build and test with fixtures, fake HTTP servers on localhost and temp dirs. Never call the real Ollama, never run the benchmark, never read or write runs/, data/, out/ or eval/, never edit briefs, bench/glb/eval_subjects.json or prompts/. Never commit. Assembly stays a quality signal, never a validity failure reason. Never type the literal completion tag except when every criterion holds.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use fixtures under tests/fixtures and mocked HTTP. Never call Baseten, Meta, Hugging Face or any remote service from a story, a test or a script you run. The only network use allowed is `npm install` and `.venv/bin/pip install` of packages the story names.
Never commit, push, tag or publish. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never delete, overwrite or reformat anything under data/, out/, eval/, .env or .venv. They are the owner's data (a long Glimmer generation run may be writing data/raw right now). Tests write only to temporary directories.

Do not start long jobs. Any command that would run more than about 5 minutes (corpus generation, training, GGUF conversion, evals) is written as a script plus docs and left for the owner. A live smoke call to the local Ollama is allowed only if the story says so, with at most 2 briefs, and must skip cleanly when Ollama is down. Never rent GPUs or run `runpodctl` with anything that creates a pod.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests and the doc the story names. Do not change prompts/system.txt: every existing raw answer was generated against it.

Match the surrounding code: short comments that explain why, argparse CLIs, resumable file-per-item outputs, no new dependency the story does not name. Python runs with `.venv/bin/python`; Node scripts are ESM `.mjs` (Node 22).
Three.js stays pinned at 0.160.0 and the validator keeps serving the local copy in place of the CDN URL.
Python scripts must stay importable without heavy deps: import torch, transformers, trl or peft only inside functions or under `if __name__ == '__main__'` so pytest can import them.
Record only real results. Never invent pass rates, token counts, timings or costs; where a number is unknown write 'not measured'.
Debug output goes to data/ or a temp dir, never into scripts/ or docs/.
If the spec is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in `notes`. If you cannot finish a story, set `notes` to why and stop; do not mark it passing.

The completion tag is matched literally by the harness. Write it only when every acceptance criterion holds. When a criterion cannot hold yet, never type the tag, not even inside a sentence saying you are not using it; write 'no completion signal this iteration' instead.
